$comment: Evidence manifest (Stage 1 Remediation, spec Крок C). Every evidence citation in protocol/registers.canonical.json's 'evidence' arrays cites a source_id from this file. tools/protocol/lib/semantic-checks.js resolves each citation against this manifest AND the two normalized indices (workbook_index.json, upstream_index.json) — a non-empty locator string is not accepted as proof by itself; the address/claim must actually be present in the corresponding index.

sources.note: No official JK manufacturer protocol document was available anywhere in this environment (no network path to one, none supplied by the user, none found in the repository). This source_id exists so its ABSENCE is a recorded, machine-checkable fact — 'confirmed_official' verification_status can never be assigned while this entry's status is 'unavailable'.

sources.provenance: User-supplied local file. Exact capture methodology/session log (whether it was produced from a live device read, and by what tool) is NOT independently confirmed in this environment — graded as workbook evidence (not hardware-capture evidence) for that reason.
sources.note: 129 rows total, 117 rows carry a non-empty address cell, 113 unique 0xNNNN address tokens (re-verified 2026-09-09 via build_workbook_index.py, matching the independent review's own count).

sources.commit_message: Add and align cell voltage sensors in JK-PB modbus example (#1013)
sources.provenance: Pinned upstream implementation snapshot at the exact commit recorded by commit_sha; the firmware build uses the same immutable revision.
sources.note: A register present in this index may be (a) a real implemented ESPHome entity (an 'address:' YAML key), which additionally corroborates it was actually read/written by upstream's own firmware, or (b) present ONLY inside upstream's own inline register-table comment with no implementing entity (e.g. 0x12E4 — upstream documents 'BatVol 0.01V' as a comment but never wires an entity to it). Both are recorded as evidence of the ADDRESS/FIELD MEANING claim; only (a) additionally supports an 'implemented upstream too' claim. See each address's entries in upstream_index.json (kind: 'yaml_address_key' marks case (a)).

sources.locator_base: batterylifepo4.yaml / jk_bms.js (this repository, this exact working tree)
sources.note: Evidence of what THIS project implements, never proof of protocol correctness on its own (spec section 3, tier 4 — lowest trust). A field with ONLY this source is 'single_source' / 'implementation_only_unverified', never 'confirmed_multiple_sources', regardless of how many places in the implementation happen to agree with each other (batterylifepo4.yaml and jk_bms.js are not independent of one another — both were authored together).

sources.session_scope: Read-only GET/SSE session against jk-bms.local (real device, IP 192.168.27.43 at capture time). No POST/write of any kind was performed.
sources.note: Per Крок C's hardware-evidence rule: a valid decoded number on the wire from this session confirms the register RESPONDS and that the DECODE (scale/sign/unit) produces a plausible physical value — it does NOT by itself confirm write semantics, enum meaning, or any RW claim. Device identity (manufacturer_device_id = 'JK-PB2A16S15P') is a MODEL/hardware-identity claim, not a BMS firmware-version claim — see protocol/registers.canonical.json's version_context block.
